chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the Greater Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'Greater Hajj' is specifically identified as Yawm al-Nahr (the Day of Sacrifice) on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, distinguishing it from the broader ritual period. This definition highlights the centrality of the sacrifice (Qurbani) and the stoning of the Jamarat as the climactic acts that complete the pilgrimage, a view supported by Shia jurists who emphasize the completion of the Hajj rites on this day. The hadith serves to clarify terminological distinctions in fiqh, ensuring pilgrims understand that the primary obligation of 'Hajj' is consummated on this specific day.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Zareeh,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The Greater Hajj is on the day of the Sacrifice’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd af-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the greater al-Hajj is the day of offering sacrifice.”
